Get started

Install Sigma Loop for your host, then run /sigma-init once in each repository you want it to work on.

Before you start

You need git, bash and python3 (standard library only). The GitHub CLI gh, logged in, is optional: it is needed for GitHub issues as the backlog, a Projects board, or a pull request per goal. A local-files backlog needs none of it.

HostInstallInit flagStatus
Claude Codeplugin marketplacenoneFully validated
Codexplugin marketplace--codexPartly validated
Cursorclone the repository--cursorExperimental
Antigravityclone the repository--antigravityExperimental, never run

Claude Code

Fully validated

From a terminal:

claude plugin marketplace add https://github.com/Agrim-Intelligence/sigma
claude plugin install sigmaloop@sigmaloop

Restart the session. Then, from the root of the repository you want Sigma to work on:

/sigma-init --demo
/sigma-loop

--demo queues a runnable demo goal, and /sigma-loop runs it through all the phases. No host flag is needed on Claude Code.

Codex

Partly validated
codex plugin marketplace add https://github.com/Agrim-Intelligence/sigma
codex plugin add sigmaloop@sigmaloop

Then run the init skill with the --codex flag, so AGENTS.md carries the standing rules:

/sigma-init --codex --demo

Or run its flow directly from the root of your repository, with <installed-sigma> the installed plugin directory:

python3 <installed-sigma>/skills/sigma-init/scripts/init_flow.py . --codex --demo

Measured: the install and the first loop command ran in a real Codex session. Not measured: a complete Codex goal through to a merged pull request. See Hosts.

Cursor

Experimental

Cursor has no plugin install. Sigma runs from a clone of the repository, which is your <installed-sigma>. From the root of your own repository:

git clone https://github.com/Agrim-Intelligence/sigma <installed-sigma>
python3 <installed-sigma>/skills/sigma-init/scripts/init_flow.py . --cursor --demo

The --cursor flag writes the Cursor rule files that carry the seven-phase discipline.

Measured: the scaffolding is unit-tested. Not measured: a run inside a live Cursor session. See Hosts.

Antigravity

Experimental, never run

As with Cursor, Sigma runs from a clone of the repository, which is your <installed-sigma>. From the root of your own repository:

git clone https://github.com/Agrim-Intelligence/sigma <installed-sigma>
python3 <installed-sigma>/skills/sigma-init/scripts/init_flow.py . --antigravity

The --antigravity flag writes the same managed block in AGENTS.md that --codex writes, and nothing else. It is opt-in.

Measured: the scaffold is unit-tested. Not measured: that Antigravity loads or follows it, hooks, MCP, workflows, subagents, or a goal run end to end. See Hosts.

What /sigma-init does

Run it once in every repository, on every host. It is safe to re-run: it does not ask an answered question again.

  • Checks git and gh access.
  • Asks where your backlog lives (local goal files or GitHub issues) and which command runs your tests.
  • Scaffolds the .sdlc folder and ends by printing the next command to run.

On Codex and Cursor there is no interactive question: the flow prints each open one as an [ask] line with the flag that answers it.
